beats.text: It's on the tip of my tongue.
In a classic study, people read definitions of rare words. When they got stuck, they often still knew the first letter. Or how many syllables.
So the word is in there. Just not all at once.
And it's universal. Of fifty-one languages surveyed, forty-five have a phrase for it.
A small hint, like the first sound, often unlocks it.

sources: Brown & McNeill (1966). The 'tip of the tongue' phenomenon. Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior 5. In TOT states people identified first letter and number of syllables above chance.
Schwartz (1999). Sparkling at the end of the tongue. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 6: 45 of 51 languages have a TOT idiom. Priming with first sounds aids retrieval. Via Wikipedia 'Tip of the tongue'.
